site.name: BoltGet
site.description: A download manager built for speed. Splits every file across many connections and resumes where it stopped, even after a crash.

footer.license: GPL-3.0-or-later. No ads, no account, no telemetry.

home.title: BoltGet: every byte, at full speed
home.description: A download manager built for speed. Splits every file across many connections and keeps each one busy until the last byte.
home.label: Download manager
home.headline: Every byte, at full speed.
home.sentence: Splits every file across many connections and keeps each one busy until the last byte.
home.status: v0.1 is the engine and the command-line tool. The Windows app arrives in v0.2.

stage.title: The BoltGet arrow lights up row by row, then a progress bar fills in segments that split in two as connections finish. A simulation, not a real download.
stage.staticLabel: One file, six segments, finished together.

fast.title: Fast
fast.body: {lab} MiB/s median on a 1 GiB file over loopback, and {cdn} MiB/s from a public CDN over a home line. Measured on {date}.

resume.title: Never loses progress
resume.body: Progress is saved only once the bytes are on disk. Kill it mid-download and it resumes where it stopped: 1,000 kill-and-resume cycles in testing, every file byte-identical.

browser.title: Catches downloads from the browser
browser.body: An extension for Chrome, Edge and Firefox hands downloads to BoltGet with their cookies and referrer, so signed links keep working. Arrives in v0.3.

segmentation.title: Dynamic segmentation
segmentation.body: When a connection finishes early, it takes over half of the largest remaining part, so every connection finishes together.

adaptive.title: Adaptive connections
adaptive.body: Starts with 4 connections and adds more only while they make the download faster. Backs off when a server asks it to.

refresh.title: Link refresh
refresh.body: Signed link expired at 97%? Give it a new one. BoltGet checks it is the same file and continues instead of starting over.

limits.title: Speed limits
limits.body: Per download and global, changed without reconnecting.

checksums.title: Checksums
checksums.body: SHA-256, SHA-512, SHA-1 or MD5, plus digests the server sends. Hashed while it downloads, so there is no wait at the end.

network.title: Proxies and cookies
network.body: HTTP, HTTPS and SOCKS5 proxies, browser cookies.txt files matched per request, HTTP Basic auth.

cli.heading: Scriptable from the first release
cli.body: Documented exit codes and line-delimited JSON for every state change.
cli.caption: Commands from the v0.1 command-line tool.

cta.heading: Build it, run it, measure it.
cta.body: The v0.1 preview builds from source with Rust on Windows and Linux. boltget bench measures it on your own network.

bench.title: Benchmarks
bench.description: How BoltGet's download times are measured, with dated results, the comparison with IDM and links to the raw data.
bench.label: Measured {date}
bench.lede: Every number on this page is read from a published run, with the raw data in the repository. Nothing is estimated or rounded in BoltGet's favour. A difference is claimed only when the run-to-run spreads do not overlap.
bench.resultsNote: Wall-clock seconds, {runs} measured runs per configuration after {warmup} warm-up run.

verdict.faster: Every adaptive BoltGet run was faster than every IDM run.
verdict.slower: Every IDM run was faster than every adaptive BoltGet run.
verdict.overlap: The spreads overlap, so no difference is claimed.

compare.title: BoltGet and IDM
compare.description: What BoltGet and Internet Download Manager each do today, what BoltGet has measured against IDM, and how IDM concepts map to BoltGet.
compare.label: Comparison
compare.lede: Internet Download Manager is a mature, capable download manager. This page sets out what each one does and what has been measured, so the facts can speak.
compare.statusNote: BoltGet is at v0.1: the engine and the command-line tool. Rows with a milestone are planned, not shipped.
compare.unknownNote: Unknown: we could not confirm it either way. If you know, please open an issue with a source.

bench.heading: Measured download times
bench.body: Both tools at their defaults, medians of {runs} runs on {date}. The benchmark page has the spreads, a fixed 8-connection BoltGet configuration and the raw data.

connections.boltget: Adaptive by default; -c N fixes the count, --max-connections caps it. Available now.

limiter.boltget: --limit on a download, boltget config set limit for all of them. Available now.

browser.boltget: The BoltGet extension for Chrome, Edge and Firefox (v0.3).

import.boltget: Import is being investigated for v1.0.

statement.label: How it works
statement.body: It starts with four connections and adds more only while they make the download faster. When one finishes early, it takes over half of the largest part left, so every connection finishes together.
